extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their attorneys involved in appeals at the European Patent Office (EPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for filing and prosecuting an appeal against an EPO decision, covering eligibility, timing, required content, procedural steps, and special topics (oral proceedings, admissibility of new arguments, Enlarged Board referrals, acceleration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a person who was a party to the first instance proceedings may appeal against a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successors in title to a patent/patent application/party to the proceedings must be considered carefully as can have a big impact on the filing of an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effect requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must be adversely affected by the decision in order to be able to file an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPO takes this to mean that the decision must disagree with an explicit request of that party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision requirement (what is appealable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word ‘decision’ is important, as a document that does not decide anything cannot be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only acts that constitute a decision (i.e., determine rights/obligations or grant/refuse requests) give rise to an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of appeal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be ex parte (between the EPO and the applicant only) or inter partes (between the applicant, the EPO, and one or more third parties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware which mode applies to your case since participation/opportunity to be heard differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Board of Appeal decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal proceedings are the last instance of proceedings before the EPO; the decision reached by the Board of Appeal is final and cannot be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan strategy accordingly — there is no further appeal within the EPO system from the Board's final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Board of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal proceedings are conducted before a Board of Appeal, which consists of at least three members of the EPO that are completely unrelated to the members of the EPO whose decision is being appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board is independent from the first-instance members who issued the contested decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal must be filed within two months from the date the decision is notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification date is the date on the letter from the EPO, plus the EPO’s ten day postal rule; this time period is not extensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal must detail the name and address of the party filing the appeal, and set out in brief the decision being appealed and the extent of the appeal (for example all or part of the decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure the notice clearly identifies the contested decision and the scope to avoid admissibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee and timing for notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal carries an official fee of slightly over €1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the fee and the notice of appeal must reach the EPO before the deadline, or the appeal is deemed not to have been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds (time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must be supported by a statement of grounds, which must be filed within four months from the date the decision is notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important to set out as full a case as possible initially; mere assertion that the decision is wrong is insufficient — legal and factual reasons why the decision should be set aside must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive content required in grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of grounds must include legal and factual reasons why the decision should be set aside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full case at the outset: explain the errors in fact or law and provide necessary evidence/arguments rather than only stating disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of new arguments, amendments and prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: New arguments, amendments and even prior art can be raised on appeal but the Board of Appeal will always determine whether these should be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board considers fairness to all parties when deciding admission; be prepared to justify late-filed material and address potential objections on admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting oral proceedings early
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings should be requested early in the proceedings to ensure that opportunity for argument in person is kept open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early request preserves the chance for in-person argument; otherwise the opportunity may be foreclosed by procedural developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory revision by the deciding division
rubrics_metrics.description: The division that made the decision under appeal will review the appeal filed and their own decision; if the appeal addresses all of the issues that lead to their adverse decision, that division can allow the appeal and overturn the earlier decision (known as interlocutory revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory revision can resolve the appeal without referral to the Board of Appeal; ensure grounds clearly address the division's reasons if aiming for interlocutory revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board assessment of admissibility and allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Appeal will assess both the allowability and the admissibility of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPC states the Board ‘shall invite the parties, as often as necessary, to file observations’. The Board usually issues an opinion, allows parties to comment, may issue further opinions, and may summon to oral proceedings; this exchange can take years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to comment on Board opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will usually send the applicant an opinion on the appeal, and the applicant will be given an opportunity to comment on the Board’s opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect iterative opinions and responses; prepare timely, substantive replies to influence the Board's view before oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and possibility of long duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchange of opinions and steps before summons to oral proceedings can take a number of years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings can be lengthy; plan client expectations and consider acceleration requests when legitimate reasons exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings can be accelerated but only if the applicant can give a legitimate reason why acceleration might be preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example legitimate reason: a pending infringement action. Prepare evidence/justification if seeking expedited handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged Board of Appeal referrals — scope and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, a Board of Appeal will refer a question to the Enlarged Board of Appeal; the enlarged board is not a higher instance court and is only able to decide questions relating to the uniform application of law, or the interpretation of law, not questions relating to the particular issues of a case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A referral is not an additional avenue of appeal; appeal proceedings will be suspended while the Enlarged Board reaches a decision, and the answer is remitted to the Board to allow proceedings to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and costs at appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Appeal has the power to grant any remedy that could have been granted by the Division whose decision is under appeal (such as grant or refusal of a patent application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party usually pays its own costs; be mindful that remedies available mirror those of the first instance division.
